title: Etale normal forms for a nodal family with etale markings
statement: Let $X,Y$ be locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth], $(Y,T)$ a log regular pair with divisorial log structure $M_Y$ [def-trf-log-regular-pair], and $f:X\to Y$ flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty connected one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Suppose $f$ is smooth over $Y\setminus T$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor, meaning its ideal is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], etale over $Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and supported in the relative smooth locus. At every geometric point $x$ over $y$, after taking etale neighbourhoods $U\to X$ and $V\to Y$, with $U\to V$ over $f$, the following normal forms are available. At a smooth unmarked point one may arrange $D\cap U=\varnothing$ and $U\to V$ smooth. At a marked point there is an etale $V$-morphism $U\to\mathbf A^1_V$ with coordinate $z$ for which $D\cap U$ is exactly $z=0$. At a nonsmooth point one may arrange $D\cap U=\varnothing$ and an etale $V$-morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}_V(\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h))$, sending the chosen point to $u=v=0$, where $h\in\mathcal O_V$ is a function invertible on $V\setminus T_V$, $T_V=V\times_Y T$. Consequently $h$ is a section of $M_Y|_V$, and after a further etale refinement there is a fine saturated chart $c:P\to M_Y|_V$ and an expression $h=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$, with $\varepsilon\in\mathcal O_V^\times$, $a\in P$, and $\alpha:P\to\mathcal O_V$ the chart structure map. All these neighbourhoods may be refined to carry a fine saturated chart of the base.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; ILO Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 proof, printed pp. 70--71, equation (1.a) and the smooth-locus case. The marked coordinate is the smooth relative curve coordinate adapted to the etale Cartier marking.

proof.text: Every geometric fibre is purely one-dimensional: a zero-dimensional irreducible component of a locally Noetherian one-dimensional connected scheme would be a clopen isolated point (a component meeting another component is not maximal irreducible), contradicting connectedness and dimension one. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to obtain the open relative smooth locus. At a smooth point outside the closed divisor $D$, restrict to its intersection with $X\setminus D$. This gives the smooth unmarked case.

source.place: Tags 0C59/0C5A; smooth case of ILO VI Proposition 1.9.

proof.text: At a marked point restrict to the relative smooth locus. The closed pair $D\hookrightarrow X$ is smooth over the base, since the marking is etale. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates]. The fibre dimensions one and zero give $a=0,b=1$; its Cartesian coordinate-subspace square is exactly the scheme-theoretic equation $z=0$ for $D$.

At a nonsmooth point apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model], whose pure-dimension hypothesis was checked in step 1. This gives $U,V,h,e:U\to W$. By [lem-trf-nodal-model-etale-smooth-locus], lift the prescribed geometric point to $U$; its image in $W$ has $u=v=0$. Remove the inverse image of $D$, which contains no nonsmooth point, and keep that lift. The same lemma identifies smoothness for $U\to V$ with smoothness for $f$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; identification of the pointed node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-chart-boundary-shrinking] with $T_V=V\times_YT$. Step 3 supplies its chosen node and identifies the smooth loci, so smoothness of $f$ off $T$ supplies its smoothness hypothesis. For its closed set $Z$, the image of $N\setminus e(U)$ under $N\simeq V(h)$, replace $V$ by $V\setminus Z$ and $U$ by its inverse image. The lemma retains the chosen point and makes $h$ invertible on $V\setminus T_V$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, equation (1.a): h invertible away from T.

proof.text: In both smooth cases initially take $V=Y$ and the given geometric lift into the open $U$. In the nodal case $h$ is invertible on $V\times_Y(Y\setminus T)=V\setminus T_V$ by step 4, so by the definition $M_Y=\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_{Y\setminus T}^\times$ in [def-trf-log-regular-pair] it is a section of $M_Y|_V$. At the geometric point of $V$ obtained from the chosen lift in $U$, apply [lem-trf-divisorial-section-chart-factorization] to $(h)$ in the nodal case and to the empty list in the smooth cases. It gives the fs base chart and, in the nodal case, $h=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$. Pull $U$ back to this pointed etale refinement of $V$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] preserves the etale chart maps; clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] preserves their etale composites to $X$. The two retained lifts agree over $V$, so their fibre-product lift maps to the prescribed point of $X$. The coordinate squares and omission of $D$ pull back, and clause (1) of [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] preserves smooth relative dimension one. Thus every case has the asserted base chart.
